title: stage-partitioned-rollback-policy-with-multi-metric-safeguards
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: incidents in the last quarter showed that single-metric rollback (typically error-rate) was too coarse for several classes of regressions: subtle semantic regressions that didn't immediately spike errors but harmed downstream quality, and transient infra-induced latency spikes that recovered quickly but caused noisy rollbacks. This PR introduces a stage-partitioned rollback policy that evaluates multiple signals (latency p90, request error rate, end-to-end QA eval score) per traffic partition (cohorts: paid/free, beta/opt-in) and triggers automated mitigations with cooldowns, quarantines, and optional human-in-the-loop escalation.

What this changes (high level):
- New RolloutPolicy CRD extension: "stagePartitions" field lets operators declare per-stage partitions with metric guards and weighted thresholds.
- Multi-metric evaluator: configurable rule engine that combines metrics with logical gates (AND/OR) and supports hysteresis windows to avoid flapping.
- Partition-aware automatic actions: graceful rollback to prior model variant, divert partition to a warm fallback model, or transition partition to shadow mode for traffic capture and replay.
- Quarantine and replay support: when a partition is quarantined an audit event and traffic capture snapshot are created for offline investigation and automated replay testing.
- Console + alerting hooks: new UI widgets to visualize partition-level metrics and an opt-in policy simulator in Console for dry-run validation.

Implementation notes:
- Controller changes: rollout-controller has a new stage-partition reconciliation loop that evaluates metric windows (default 10m primary window with 3m sampling stride). We added per-partition state persisted in the rollout status to track cooldowns, consecutive breaches, and last-action timestamps.
- Metrics ingestion: extended the metrics adapter to fetch model-level latency/e2e QA scores from Observability (Prometheus for latency, internal eval-store API for QA scores). Aggregation uses a sliding window reservoir to avoid bias when partitions have low qps.
- Safety: all automatic actions are gated by a feature flag (rollout.partitioned.auto_mitigate) and require a minimum sample count; actions emit structured audit logs and create a rollback runbook link.
- Backwards compatibility: existing RolloutPolicy schemas remain valid; controllers treat old policies as single-partition defaults.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for evaluator logic and CRD parsing (added ~40 tests).
- Integration tests: simulated canary runs against the perf-canary harness with synthetic regressions (semantic degradation and latency bursts).
- Load test: 1k rps sustained on perf-lab to validate aggregation when partitions have skewed traffic.
- Staging rollout: dry-run enabled on staging for 48h; we used the Console policy simulator to validate thresholds and observed no false positives.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy to staging with feature flag off.
2) Enable dry-run for a subset of rollouts (no actions) and validate metric collection for 24h.
3) Canary in prod: apply to low-risk customers (opt-in beta cohort) with auto-mitigate disabled for 72h.
4) Gradual enable of auto_mitigate: 1% -> 5% -> 20% of eligible rollouts over a week.

Operational notes for on-call:
- When a partition mitigation occurs, a PagerDuty incident is created for SEV-3 by default; SEV-2 if mitigations affect >10% of paid traffic.
- Runbook included at: https://linear.app/ENG-3120/runbooks/partitioned-rollback (linked in audit entry).

Related tickets: ENG-3120, ENG-3299, PM-2042.

Checklist: [x] CRD schema bump documented; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] Console changes behind feature flag; [x] migration notes added to docs; [x] security review completed.

Notes on differences from prior approaches: this PR focuses on guardrails at the traffic partition level (not only at global rollout level). It reduces noisy global rollbacks by isolating mitigations to the affected cohorts and enabling controlled replay to validate quality regressions before a full rollback.

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Can we tolerate partitions with very low QPS? The sliding-window reservoir addresses bias but add a minimum-sample check to avoid noisy decisions — addressed in multimetric.go (added minSamples config).
Lina Zhou: Add explicit audit events for every automatic action so security/compliance can trace mitigations. — added structured audit log events and a link to the replay snapshot in the status.
Tom Higgs: Suggest exposing an "opt-out" label for customers who prefer manual rollouts. — added an optOut label check in reconciliation and documented in examples.
